articles.title: Turkey pushes KAAN stealth jet as tensions with Israel deepen
articles.body:
Breadcrumb
Turkey pushes KAAN stealth jet as tensions with Israel deepen
Turkey is accelerating development of its fifth-generation KAAN fighter jet as Ankara seeks greater military independence amid increasingly open tensions with Israel and Israeli strikes targeting potential Turkish military expansion in Syria.
The Turkish-built fighter is intended eventually to provide Ankara with a sovereign alternative to the US-made F-35, a programme Turkey was expelled from after acquiring Russia's S-400 air defence system.
Turkey had been a partner in the F-35 programme and planned to operate the stealth fighter before Washington removed Ankara and later imposed sanctions over the S-400 purchase.
The setback left Turkey without an operational fifth-generation fighter, while Israel operates the F-35I Adir, giving it a significant advantage in stealth air power.
KAAN, developed by Turkish Aerospace Industries (TUSAS), is intended to narrow that gap while reducing Ankara's dependence on foreign suppliers for advanced military capabilities.
The aircraft's first prototype flew in February 2024, while a newer prototype began taxi tests in July as Turkey moves towards a more advanced phase of testing.
Turkish officials say the aircraft was designed domestically from the ground up as part of a decades-long effort to establish an independent combat aircraft industry.
KAAN is being developed with stealth, internal weapons carriage, advanced radar, electronic warfare and sensor fusion.
These technologies intend to make the aircraft harder to detect and allow pilots to combine information from multiple sensors into a single battlefield picture.
However, one of the programme's biggest remaining challenges is the engine.
KAAN's prototypes and initial production aircraft rely on US-made General Electric F110 engines.
Turkey is developing the TF35000, a domestic 35,000-pound-thrust-class engine intended eventually to power KAAN, but Turkish Aerospace has indicated that integration is targeted for around 2032.
Developing an advanced fighter engine is particularly difficult because it requires technologies including heat-resistant alloys, turbine cooling, precision manufacturing and sophisticated digital controls.
Until Turkey succeeds, KAAN will reduce some forms of foreign dependence while retaining another through its reliance on US propulsion.
Israeli aggression raises the stakes
That vulnerability has become more significant as relations between Turkey and Israel have deteriorated.
Syria has emerged as a major arena of tension since the fall of Bashar al-Assad in December 2024 and the emergence of a new government closely aligned with Ankara.
In April 2025, Israel struck the T4, Palmyra and Hama airbases after Turkish military teams had inspected the facilities as Ankara considered expanding its military presence in Syria.
Sources told Reuters at the time that the attack rendered T4 effectively unusable, with one regional intelligence official describing the strikes as a message that Israel would not accept an expanded Turkish presence.
Tensions escalated further in August, when Israel bombed the Abu al-Duhur airbase in northwestern Syria after claiming Turkish troops were preparing to deploy there.
Turkey and Syria denied that any permanent Turkish deployment was planned.
US envoy Tom Barrack later said US intelligence had examined the Israeli claim and concluded that Turkey was not moving military assets into the base.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has nevertheless warned that Israel would not tolerate an expanding Turkish military presence in Syria.
Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz has also warned President Recep Tayyip Erdogan against what he described as "dangerous" military moves in Syria and against testing Israel's willingness to act.
Israel has also opposed Turkey regaining access to the F-35.
Netanyahu said in July that he opposed a possible US sale of the aircraft to Ankara, arguing that it could alter the regional balance of power.
President Donald Trump has signalled a willingness to reconsider Turkey's access to the F-35, although political and legal obstacles remain.
For Ankara, Israel's fifth-generation air advantage, its strikes on Syrian military infrastructure linked to possible Turkish deployments and its opposition to Turkey acquiring F-35s add further strategic importance to KAAN.
A mature KAAN equipped with a Turkish engine, radar, electronic warfare systems and weapons would give Ankara a degree of independent high-end air power it currently lacks.
Israel, however, already operates a mature and combat-tested F-35 fleet, while KAAN remains in development.
Turkey is also seeking foreign partners for the programme, with Saudi Arabia in advanced discussions over possible involvement.
If Ankara succeeds in combining KAAN with a domestically produced engine and indigenous combat systems, the fighter could significantly reduce Turkey's reliance on Washington while beginning to narrow one of Israel's most important technological advantages over it.

articles.title: Trump official says ‘there may not be a nuclear agreement’ with Iran
articles.body:
Trump official says ‘there may not be a nuclear agreement’ with Iran
US Energy Secretary Chris Wright’s comments could signal that US hopes for a nuclear deal are dimming.
As the United States and Iran resume trading attacks, a top US official has publicly downplayed the chances of one of President Donald Trump’s initial key objectives in the US and Israel’s war on Iran: getting a signed nuclear agreement.
During an interview on Sunday with US channel ABC News, the US Energy Secretary, Chris Wright, said “there may not” be a nuclear deal, signalling that the US may pivot instead to launching strikes against any Iranian efforts to build nuclear infrastructure.

- list 2 of 3Iran President Pezeshkian calls for unity as US ramps up economic pressure
- list 3 of 3US, Iran engaged in tanker war: Where is the months-long conflict headed?
“It may be simply destroying their capabilities to do it,” Wright said on ‘ABC This Week’ about Iran’s ambitions to obtain a nuclear weapon.
The US has previously targeted facilities it said had been used to support Iran’s nuclear programme. Iran has always maintained that it is developing a nuclear power programme only and does not have plans to build a nuclear weapon.
Later, when pressed by the show’s co-host, Martha Raddatz, on whether the US would resort to continued bombing instead of diplomacy, Wright defended US actions in Iran.
“They don’t have the capability to build more missiles,” Wright said. “We’re degrading their capacity to develop nuclear weapons and, ultimately, to deliver them if they develop them.”
However, the former oil executive whose agency oversees the US stockpile of nuclear weapons said that a deal with Iran could be possible under new leadership.
“An agreement may await the next administration in Iran,” he said. “We simply don’t know that.”
The Trump administration official’s comments could signal that US hopes for a nuclear deal are dimming and slipping further out of reach.
After the memorandum of understanding between the US and Iran collapsed in July, attacks paused, then resumed, coupled with Iranian closures of the Strait of Hormuz and US naval blockade.
Despite recent exchanges of intense fire between US and Iranian forces, the White House has attempted to minimise the conflict in public remarks.
On Friday, Trump sought to downplay the war in Iran, calling it “small potatoes”. While at a White House news briefing on Thursday, Vice President JD Vance appeared to suggest that the conflict had cooled and to shrug off an alleged US attack on a wedding in southern Iran, saying “sometimes things happen“.
At a White House briefing this week, Vance said of the conflict that he “wouldn’t call it a war” and there was “no active shooting right now”.
Without offering specifics, Wright on Sunday said the US would “get the job done” in Iran and other nations would be offering their help to bring an end to the war.
“We will work in cooperation with our allies in the region,” Wright said. “I think you’ll see countries from around the world joining this effort as well.”
Al Jazeera has reached out to the White House for comment.

articles.title: US envoys visit Kyiv to revive Ukraine-Russia talks to end war
articles.body:
U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff held talks Sunday with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to end the war with Russia, a day after they met with Russia's Vladimir Putin.
The Americans arrived in the Ukrainian capital Kyiv by train, hoping to revive negotiations to end Europe's worst conflict since World War II following a summer of escalation.
Zelenskyy published a video of his meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump's son-in-law Kushner and business partner Witkoff in central Kyiv, saying: "Talks have begun."
Witkoff and Kushner had visited Moscow eight times but had not held talks in Kyiv until now, despite the city enduring deadly strikes since Russia's February 2022 invasion.
Ukraine's top security officials and negotiators were also present and several European national security advisors.
Zelenskyy showed the U.S. envoys Kyiv's historic Saint Sophia's Cathedral, which stands opposite the SBU security building that a Russian drone hit Friday.
Moscow's invasion of Ukraine has killed hundreds of thousands of people and displaced millions.
Witkoff and Kushner met with Putin on Saturday to "advance President Trump's agenda of peace in the war in Ukraine," a White House official said.
"The two sides discussed substantive plans for next steps, which will be announced in the coming weeks, and look forward to equally productive meetings tomorrow in Ukraine."
Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov called the talks "extremely frank," saying the Americans "put forward a number of ideas on possible routes to a settlement," but did not elaborate.
The Russian side told the Americans that Moscow was "confident" it could achieve its military goals of seizing the rest of eastern Ukraine, Ushakov added.
Both Russia and Ukraine had vowed not to strike each other's capitals for three days during the Americans' visit.
Zelenskyy Sunday said Ukraine was "ready for the conversation."
"Ukraine has always been and will remain constructive," the wartime leader said on social media ahead of their visit.
The country's airspace has been closed since Moscow launched the war, and visiting leaders have been arriving by train.
In televised comments before the talks, Putin said Russia would ensure the safety of the envoys in Kyiv.
"We will do everything that depends on us to ensure the safety of the negotiation process and mediators such as yourselves," Putin told Witkoff and Kushner.
Earlier Saturday, Putin had thanked Trump for persisting in his efforts to end the war despite the task being "not simple."
Of the envoys' trip to Kyiv, he said: "No matter what happens next, contacts of this kind are undoubtedly always beneficial."
Trump said Friday that his envoys were bringing a "proposal" to end the fighting.
"We have an idea for peace," he said, without elaborating.
U.S. efforts have so far not led to a breakthrough in the war and peace efforts have stalled.
Russia has occupied large swathes of eastern and southern Ukraine, and Putin has insisted Moscow is intent on seizing the rest of eastern Ukraine.
Despite the cease-fire pledges for the capital cities, fighting continued elsewhere.
Ukraine's air force said Russia attacked overnight with 108 drones and missiles, while Moscow said it shot down 258 drones.
On Saturday, Putin said he "noted that the Ukrainian side significantly reduced" its strikes on Russia and Moscow.
However, Kyiv said Russian strikes killed 10 people across the country Saturday, including a child and family members in the Kharkiv region and two people outside Kyiv.

articles.title: Satellite Imagery Confirms Damage to Millerovo Air Base
articles.body:
Satellite imagery has confirmed damage to two radars, the technical and operational unit and an ammunition depot at Millerovo air base in the Rostov region.
Satellite images showing the aftermath of the attack were published by the Dnipro OSINT project’s channel.
The attack was carried out overnight on August 30 by the 1st Center of the Unmanned Systems Forces using FP-1 drones. Millerovo and Yeysk air bases were targeted in the attack.
According to the satellite imagery, an ammunition depot, RSP-27 and Nebo-SV radars, and the technical and operational unit were damaged at Millerovo air base. The unit and ammunition depot were completely destroyed.
Millerovo military air base, located 170 kilometers from the line of contact, is used by Russian forces to launch Shahed-type strike drones and carry out airstrikes.
Millerovo air base is known to host the Russian 31st Fighter Aviation Regiment of the Russian Aerospace Forces, equipped with Su-30SM and Su-35 fighter jets.
The destroyed RSP-27 is an airfield surveillance radar that, in addition to detecting aerial targets, is an integral element of air traffic control.
The serious damage to the airfield’s technical and operational unit could also complicate preparations of Russian aircraft for sorties.
With the development of long-range drones, Millerovo is increasingly becoming a target of Ukrainian attacks. Several days before the 1st Center of the Unmanned Systems Forces carried out its attack. The Long-Range Strike Company of the 429th Unmanned Systems Brigade Achilles published a video of a strike.
At the time, Ukrainian troops used a RAM-2X strike drone to hit a Nebo-U radar station in the Rostov region. Ahead of the strike, a Ukrainian reconnaissance UAV conducted aerial reconnaissance of the site.
Several days earlier, the 1st Center of the Unmanned Systems Forces hit a Russian MiG-29 fighter jet at Millerovo air base.
In late August, Ukraine’s Defense Forces hit the Russian Akhtubinsk military air base in the Astrakhan region, where a Su-34 frontline bomber was damaged.

articles.body:
Sayyari: Iran’s deterrence capabilities have significantly increased after recent wars
TEHRAN — Iran’s deterrence capabilities have significantly strengthened following the country’s recent military confrontations with the United States and Israel, Rear Admiral Habibollah Sayyari, deputy chief of Iran’s Army for Coordination Affairs, said.
Reacting to recent remarks by US President Donald Trump about maintaining pressure on Iran, Sayyari said Washington’s statements reflected its inability to achieve its objectives on the battlefield.
He said strengthening Iran’s deterrence remained a central responsibility of the Armed Forces and that the military had drawn on its experience in recent conflicts to identify weaknesses and reinforce its capabilities.
“Based on the valuable experiences gained from the 12-day war jointly imposed by the United States and Israel against Iran, as well as the subsequent 40-day conflict, including what we refer to as the Ramadan War and the Hormuz War, we have made extensive efforts to address potential weaknesses and strengthen our capabilities,” Sayyari said.
“These efforts have significantly increased the country’s deterrence power,” he added.
Sayyari was also dismissive of Trump’s remarks about a possible naval and economic blockade of Iran, describing them as unfounded and repetitive.
He said Trump had repeatedly made similar claims about Iran, including that the country did not possess nuclear weapons, that its navy and air force had been destroyed, and that its economy was in severe difficulty.
“We have become accustomed to these unfounded and baseless statements,” Sayyari said.
The senior commander said US officials were well aware of Iran’s military capabilities and argued that Washington would not be able to overcome 'the combat power, resistance and national resolve of the Iranian people.'
“As long as the people remain united and stand alongside the government officials, no one can defeat Iran,” he said.
Sayyari pointed to Iran’s eight-year war with Iraq, from 1980 to 1988, known in Iran as the Sacred Defense, as a historical example of 'the Iranian people’s resilience under sustained military pressure.'
He also praised 'the continued support of the Iranian people for the Islamic Republic,' describing national unity and public resilience as important elements of Iran’s deterrence.

articles.title: Live: Trump's envoys arrive in Kyiv after 'substantive' talks with Putin
articles.body:
Although Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky described talks with US special envoy Steve Witkoff and Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner as “substantial”, he warned that the war with Russia was likely to continue this winter. The US envoys arrived in Kyiv for their first official visit on Sunday, a day after meeting Russia’s President Vladimir Putin in Moscow. Read our blog to see how the day's events unfolded.
US envoys have left Kyiv after talks with Zelensky
US President Donald Trump's two envoys have left Kyiv after talks with Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky, the country's rail service operator said Monday.
"We sent off Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner's special train," Ukrainian Railways said in a post on Telegram.
Zelensky holding more talks with Witkoff, Kushner over ‘more effective’ proposals
US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff brought new, possibly more workable proposals on ending the war with Russia to Kyiv and President Volodymyr Zelensky is holding another meeting with them in a trio format, a senior Ukrainian presidential official said.
“It’s not the same as it was before. This one now is more effective,” the source said, adding: “They’re still talking. This is actually the most important part. There are three of them now.”
Zelensky thanks US envoys for Kyiv visit
Video: ‘Cordial’ meeting with US envoys, but Zelensky ‘talking as though war will continue’
The meetings between Donald Trump’s special peace envoys and Volodymyr Zelensky in Kyiv may have been very polite and cordial, but the Ukrainian president’s comments afterward suggests that the Americans presented much of the same peace proposals as before and that Zelensky believes the war will continue for now, Gulliver Cragg, FRANCE 24’s correspondent in Ukraine explained.
Watch the full video below:
Zelensky says only leaders meeting can solve territorial issue
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said that territorial issues can only be resolved “at the level of leaders” after talks with US envoys on ending the war with Russia.
Zelensky has previously called for a meeting with Russia’s Vladimir Putin.
In pictures: President Zelensky’s press conference with US envoys
Photos: Reuters
Both Russia and Ukraine need to make ‘compromises’ for war to end, Witkoff says
US envoy Steve Witkoff said both Russia and Ukraine need to make “some compromises and narrow the issues between them” to end four years of war.
“It is very difficult but we are committed, we care and we hope all of that leads to a successful peaceful diplomatic resolution,” he said.
War looks likely to continue in winter, Zelensky says
Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky said that while there was a “positive assessment” of talks with US envoys visiting Kyiv, the war with Russia “at the moment” looked likely to continue this winter.
“We very much hope that we will be able to reach agreements with our American partners, and we are counting on the support of our European partners –if the war continues in winter, and this is how it appears at the moment – but even so, the teams today have a positive assessment of our future prospects,” he said.
Zelensky describes talks with US envoys as ‘very substantial’ 
Ukraine’s talks with US peace negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner were “very substantial”, President Volodymyr Zelensky said.
Zelensky told reporters that they discussed security and economic guarantees for Ukraine and also supplies of air-defence missiles and a winter support package. He also hoped that trilateral talks, including Ukraine, Russia and the US would restart soon.
In pictures: Trump’s envoys attend talks in Kyiv
US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, US President Donald Trump's son-in-law, attend a meeting with Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky and representatives of Britain, France and Germany in Kyiv, on September 6, 2026.
Photos: Reuters
US envoys equipped with ‘few new ideas’, looking to revive old proposals, FT reports
Citing sources, the Financial Times reports that Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have brought “few new ideas” with them to Kyiv and are mainly seeking to revive earlier proposals to end the war.
The documents the duo is presenting, the FT‘s Ukraine correspondent Christopher Miller writes on X, are updated versions of previous proposals that have been “revised to reflect the changed circumstances since peace negotiations stalled in February, at the outset of the US war with Iran”.
One of the central issues is the remaining Ukrainian-held territory in Donbas – estimated at around 25 percent – which Russia has claimed but has so far been unable to capture.
Kushner hopes talks will lead to ‘new ways to advance’ peace
“Hopefully this trip has come out with some new ways to advance forward. I think we’ve learned a lot from the trip,” US President Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner said after holding talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.
Russia says it has struck Ukrainian cargo vessel in Black Sea
The Russian defence ministry said its forces have struck a Ukrainian cargo vessel in the Black Sea, which it said was carrying military equipment supplied to the Ukrainian army by Western countries, Russian news agencies reported.
Kushner says looking forward to more progress in peace talks
The US delegation visiting Kyiv is looking forward to making more progress in peace talks aimed at ending the war in Ukraine, US envoy Jared Kushner said.
In joint statements to reporters after the first round of talks, fellow envoy Steve Witkoff said the US team had been “very encouraged” by what he described as a “substantive, important” discussion.
🎥 Ukraine-Russia talks: What are the US objectives?

We discuss this topic with our guest, John E. Herbst, director of the Eurasia Center at the Atlantic Council.
Third meeting with US envoys in Kyiv underway, now with European representatives, source says
A senior Ukrainian official, who spoke to the Associated Press on condition of anonymity, said Sunday afternoon that two rounds of discussion had taken place with the US officials, and that a third meeting with the European representatives was underway.
Much of the discussion was focused on "how to get through the winter and what can be done before then,” he said.

articles.title: Russian Ballistic Strike Shuts Down Ukraine’s Kamet Steel Plant, Killing Five Workers
articles.body:
- Category
- War in Ukraine
Russian Ballistic Strike Shuts Down Ukraine’s Kamet Steel Plant, Killing Five Workers
A Russian ballistic missile strike on the Kamet Steel plant in Kamianske, Ukraine’s Dnipropetrovsk region, killed five people, wounded four others, and forced the major steelmaking facility to suspend production.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
According to Metinvest, the plant’s parent company, on September 5, the attack occurred overnight and damaged Kamet Steel’s sinter and blast furnace operations, as well as energy and transport infrastructure across the industrial site.
Four Kamet Steel employees and one worker from a contractor were killed in the strike. Another four employees sustained injuries of varying severity and remain under medical supervision.
Only several minutes passed between the declaration of an air raid alert and the missile strike, Metinvest said, leaving some workers unable to reach shelters in time.
Oleksandr Myronenko, Metinvest’s chief operating officer, said there were no military facilities, equipment, or military production at the plant.
“Only civilians worked here, smelting iron and steel exclusively for civilian purposes,” Myronenko said.
Emergency and recovery operations are underway at the site. Specialists will be able to conduct a full assessment of the damaged equipment and infrastructure after debris removal is completed, according to the company.
Metinvest has not provided a timeline for restarting production. Kamet Steel is one of Ukraine’s major metallurgical facilities and produces pig iron, steel, and rolled products. The plant is part of Metinvest, one of the country’s largest industrial groups.
The September 5 attack marks the second time in recent weeks that a major Metinvest steel facility has halted operations following a Russian ballistic missile strike.
In August, Zaporizhstal suspended operations after a ballistic attack struck the facility shortly after an air raid alert was issued. Seven plant employees were killed and another 21 were injured in that attack.
Kamianske declared September 5 a day of mourning for those killed in the latest strike, while flags were lowered at Metinvest facilities.
The strike on Kamet Steel came during a broader Russian overnight attack on Ukraine on September 5. Russia also targeted Kyiv and Boryspil airports with Shahed-type drones, which President Volodymyr Zelenskyy linked to preparations for a possible US delegation arriving in Ukraine by air.

articles.title: Iran to tackle economic issues, says further attacks will be 'more painful'
articles.body:
Iran to tackle economic issues, says further attacks will be 'more painful'
DUBAI, Sept 6 - Iran said it will step up efforts to tackle problems created by U.S. sanctions that are crippling its economy, while a senior Iranian official warned of a "painful response" if it comes under further attack.
Six months after U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran launched the war, the conflict appears to be at a stalemate. A preliminary ceasefire accord reached in June has unravelled, and little progress has been made in diplomatic efforts to get the peace process back on track.
After a pause in military action for much of August, tit-for-tat strikes have resumed with U.S. Central Command saying it hit three Iranian tankers on Saturday after Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps launched ballistic missiles at two U.S. Navy ships.
Following the attacks, Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf said on Sunday that the U.S. should understand that the rules of the game have changed "before it is too late".
"From now on, any attack against Iran’s interests and security will receive a faster, heavier and more painful response,” he said in a speech published on his Telegram channel.
A restricted zone will be announced outside the Strait of Hormuz in coming days, Mohsen Rezaei, the secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, said on Sunday, according to state media.
He added that the zone would include areas in the Gulf. Few details were provided on the plan initially, but Rezaei said any ship entering the new zone would be added to a sanctions list.
Tehran has shown it retains the capability to attack U.S. interests in neighbouring countries and to shut down oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of global oil supplies flowed prior to the conflict.
SANCTIONS, OIL BLOCKADE SQUEEZE ECONOMY
However, the U.S. campaign to throttle Iran's economy by blockading its oil exports and stopping sanctions evasion is growing increasingly difficult to withstand, three senior Iranian sources have said.
In his speech on Sunday, Qalibaf added that alongside the military front, Iran’s main battle was now over production and people’s livelihoods.
He cited sharp currency fluctuations, inflation, unemployment and market management as major challenges, adding Iranians could tolerate hardship but not mismanagement or inaction and expected the government to act quickly.
Iran's Economy Minister Ali Madanizadeh said that Tehran planned to respond to U.S. economic pressure with reforms and rejected the notion that sanctions would cause it to change course, according to state media on Sunday.
“They speak of economic pressure and isolation, of breaking off financial ties and they think that by pressuring the economy of a country they can change the decisions of its people,” Madanizadeh said.
“I have to clarify one point: The responsibility of reforming Iran’s economy is with its government and people, not with the U.S. Treasury."
Separately, Economy Ministry Deputy Morteza Zamanian said on Sunday that the ministry's “Economic War Headquarters” was doubling down on its work to resolve problems caused by the war, according to the semi-official Tasnim news agency.
KHARG ISLAND HIT 550 TIMES IN PRIOR MONTHS, IRAN SAYS
Iran is the third-largest producer in the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and exported 90% of its crude via its Kharg Island export hub before the war. Flows have been disrupted since a U.S. blockade of Iranian oil exports began in mid-April.
U.S. Central Command said on X that as of Sunday it had redirected 92 commercial vessels, disabled three and boarded two to ensure strict compliance with its blockade.
On August 31, U.S. President Donald Trump issued a one-line social media post accompanied by an AI-generated video depicting Kharg Island being "blown to smithereens." Iranian authorities have vowed a strong response if Kharg is attacked.
In an interview aired on state TV on Sunday, Iran's Oil Minister Mohsen Paknejad said the island had been hit around 550 times in previous months but continued to operate.
Iran has also imposed a blockade on the Strait of Hormuz, creating an issue for Trump by pushing up fuel prices globally as his Republican Party heads into elections in November when control of Congress is at stake.
However, U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright said oil was getting through the waterway.
"Our transits through the Strait are averaging over 9 million barrels a day now, and with the access pipelines that go around the strait, we're probably two-thirds or more of pre-conflict flows. So Iranians are still causing trouble, but the United States Navy is winning that battle," he told CNN.
On Saturday, U.S. Central Command said it struck three Iranian vessels, including one off the coast of Kharg Island, after Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps launched ballistic missiles at two U.S. Navy ships. REUTERS

articles.title: German warship fires ballistic missile in message to Russia
articles.body:
A German warship has fired an Israeli-made LORA ballistic missile during a live test in the North Atlantic, with the German Navy saying the launch demonstrated a strike capability with a potential range beyond anything it had previously operated.
German media reports, citing a German Navy spokesman, said two German frigates had deployed to waters between Ireland and Iceland for the test on Tuesday night. Images from the exercise show a containerised launcher positioned on the deck of a German vessel. The messaging here could hardly be clearer.
By disclosing a test that had deliberately been kept secret, NATO was sending a direct signal to Moscow: European forces are developing longer-range strike options, and not every capability will be visible before it is ready. NATO Allied Joint Force Command Brunssum said the test had been kept secret until after it was completed and involved a German frigate firing the missile in the North Atlantic.
The command stated: “Kept secret. Now revealed. The German Navy just tested the Israeli LORA ballistic missile from a German frigate in the North Atlantic — quietly, deliberately and with a range of 500+ km.”
Kept secret. Now revealed. 🚀🇩🇪
The German Navy just tested the Israeli 🇮🇱 LORA ballistic missile from a German frigate in the North Atlantic — quietly, deliberately and with a range of 500+ km.
NATO 3.0 looks like this:
Europe is taking more responsibility, building serious… pic.twitter.com/K8x2JE61Gs
— NATO Allied Joint Force Command Brunssum – JFCBS (@NATOJFCBS) September 2, 2026
It added: “NATO 3.0 looks like this: Europe is taking more responsibility, building serious capabilities and keeping a few cards close to the chest. Deterrence just got a little more interesting.”
Vice Admiral Jan Christian Kaack, Inspector of the German Navy, said: “With the successful launch of a ballistic missile last night in the North Atlantic, we made naval history. I am extremely satisfied with this achievement.”
Kaack added that the system “can be successfully deployed from our units, and the potential range exceeds anything we have known before.”
In his original statement, the German Navy chief said the trial opened a new chapter for maritime deterrence and readiness, stating that the system could be operated successfully from German units and that its possible reach exceeded previous German naval capabilities.
The test was conducted with Israel Aerospace Industries’ LORA, or Long-Range Artillery Weapon System. According to IAI, the missile has a range of around 400 kilometres and an accuracy of within 10 metres, while NATO’s public account of the German test referred to a range of more than 500 kilometres. Israel Aerospace Industries said the missile was launched from an operational German vessel equipped with a command trailer and launcher. According to the company, the missile followed its planned trajectory, navigated to the target and successfully struck it, with both the weapon system and missile meeting the objectives of the trial.
Boaz Levy, Chairman of IAI, said: “This is an unprecedented achievement for IAI and the Israeli Ministry of Defense. The successful trial of the LORA missile, launched from a naval vessel and striking its target with exceptional precision, took place overnight in Germany – the country where the world’s first ballistic missile was developed.”
He added: “This trial demonstrates Israel’s technological strength and the unique cooperation between Israel and Germany. It marks another significant achievement alongside the deployment of the Arrow 3 system on German soil, further strengthening Germany’s defense and deterrence capabilities and deepening the strategic partnership between our two countries.”
IAI chief executive Guy Bar Lev said: “Israel Aerospace Industries is proud to take part in strengthening the strategic cooperation between the State of Israel and the Government of Germany. This significant milestone is underscored by the operational live-fire exercise (OPEX) of the LORA system, one of the world’s most advanced and combat-proven ballistic missile systems.”
The German Navy is using its OPEX initiative to trial technologies and operational concepts as part of its Marine 2035 and Beyond programme. The process is intended to allow new systems to be tested rapidly under conditions intended to resemble operational use as closely as possible.
The North Atlantic launch comes as Germany expands its investment in long-range strike and air and missile defence. The country has also begun fielding the Israeli-developed Arrow 3 ballistic missile defence system as part of its wider effort to strengthen national and NATO defensive capabilities.

articles.title: US Envoys Witkoff and Kushner Arrive in Kyiv for First Visit
articles.body:
US special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Kyiv on Sunday, Sept. 6, marking their first visit to Ukraine since the beginning of Russia’s full-scale invasion.
The US delegation arrived by train at Kyiv’s central railway station for direct negotiations with Ukraine’s leadership.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
A senior Ukrainian delegation met the envoys upon arrival, including Head of the Office of the President Kyrylo Budanov, First Deputy Head of the Presidential Office Sergiy Kyslytsya, Head of the Foreign Intelligence Service (SZRU) Rustem Umerov, and “Servant of the People” parliamentary faction leader Davyd Arakhamia.
“Welcome to Kyiv, representatives of the President of the United States Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner,” Umerov wrote in a statement. “We continue close coordination on further steps to end the war.”
Strategy session and preceding Kremlin talks
The arrival of the US envoys follows a preparatory strategy meeting convened by Zelensky earlier Sunday with members of Ukraine’s negotiating delegation to finalize Kyiv’s diplomatic positions.
The Kyiv talks follow a three-hour-and-10-minute meeting between Russian President Vladimir Putin and the US delegation at the Kremlin on Saturday evening, Sept. 5.
Following those discussions, Russian presidential aide Yuri Ushakov claimed that Witkoff and Kushner agreed to factor Putin’s battlefield assessments into their dialogue in Kyiv.
Kurkov: The War Could Transform Ukraine’s Political Culture
Russian officials characterized the Moscow session – which also included an informal working dinner – as “meaningful,” “frank,” and conducted in an atmosphere of mutual trust, noting that potential large-scale US-Russian commercial projects were raised alongside conflict settlement concepts.
The broader Washington delegation visiting the region included officials from the National Security Council, the State Department, and the Treasury Department.
Gene Lange, acting head of the US Treasury’s sanctions division, traveled to Moscow and held a preparatory session with Kirill Dmitriev, Putin’s special representative for economic cooperation.
While Lange did not attend the direct session with Putin, his presence underscored that sanctions policy formed part of the dialogue, despite recent assertions by US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent ruling out economic concessions without an end to the war.
At the onset of the Moscow talks, Putin confirmed that Russian forces had paused aerial strikes on Kyiv starting at midnight on Sept. 5, but rejected Ukraine’s proposal for a wider three-day frontline ceasefire.
In reciprocal coordination to safeguard the diplomatic process, Zelensky previously pledged that Ukrainian forces would refrain from striking Moscow through Monday as the US envoys conduct their meetings.

articles.title: Putin Insists on Own Terms for Peace, Vows 2026 Donbas Capture
articles.body:
Russian President Vladimir Putin entered Saturday’s Kremlin negotiations with US special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner determined to capture additional Ukrainian territory, confident that Russian forces can seize the entirety of the Donbas by the end of 2026.
“There is zero chance of reaching an agreement on the frontlin until Putin completes the capture of the rest of the Donetsk region,” a source close to the Kremlin told Reuters, noting that Putin’s confidence stems from optimistic battlefield reports submitted by his commanders.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
Western military analysts, however, view such an objective as highly improbable given the protracted and grinding pace of Russian advances. Kyiv has repeatedly and categorically rejected territorial concessions, dismissing demands to surrender the Donbas as equivalent to capitulation.
Bloomberg reported that the envoys’ latest visit yielded no indications of Moscow softening its core war objectives in Ukraine.
Sources close to the Russian leadership indicated that Putin remains willing to end the war only on Russia’s terms, with the Kremlin hardening its demands amid a belief that it holds a decisive military advantage.
The sequence and timing of the diplomatic initiative also provoked scrutiny among Western officials and analysts.
EU Ambassador to the US Jovita Neliupšienė questioned the envoys’ decision to visit Moscow before holding consultations in Kyiv.
US Sanctions Chief Joins Moscow Talks as Putin Cites War Goals
“Diplomacy really works, and we should first of all try to talk to those who are our allies,” Neliupšienė said, emphasizing that Moscow has not abandoned its original war aims and that Europe’s primary priority remains arming Ukraine for self-defense.
In contrast, Samuel Charap, a senior political scientist at the RAND Corporation, characterized the US mission as timely, warning that without active diplomatic mediation, the conflict risks rapid escalation as both sides continue to raise the stakes.
Kremlin talks and Treasury involvement
The assessments follow three hours and 10 minutes of formal discussions and a working dinner at the Kremlin on Saturday evening, Sept. 5.
Following the meeting, Russian presidential aide Yuri Ushakov claimed that the American delegation promised to factor Putin’s assessments of the conflict into their upcoming talks in Kyiv.
Russian officials characterized the session as “meaningful,” “frank,” and conducted in an atmosphere of mutual trust, while noting that discussions also addressed potential large-scale US-Russian commercial projects.
The wider US delegation included officials from the National Security Council (NSC), the State Department, and the Treasury. Gene Lange, the acting head of the sanctions division at the US Department of the Treasury, joined the mission to Moscow, participating in a preparatory meeting with Kirill Dmitriev, Putin’s special representative for economic cooperation.
While Lange did not attend the direct session with Putin, his presence signaled that US sanctions policy featured in the bilateral dialogue, despite recent statements by US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent ruling out economic concessions without an end to the war.
At the onset of the talks, Putin confirmed that Russian forces had paused aerial strikes on Kyiv starting at midnight on Sept. 5, but rejected Ukraine’s proposal for a wider three-day frontline ceasefire.
Witkoff and Kushner are scheduled to arrive in Kyiv on Sunday, Sept. 6, to meet with President Volodymyr Zelensky, who previously pledged that Ukrainian forces would refrain from striking Moscow through the end of Monday to facilitate the diplomatic mission.

articles.title: U.S. Envoys Make First Kyiv Visit Amid Ukraine War Peace Push
articles.body:
U.S. peace envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy in Kyiv on Sunday as the Trump administration renewed its push to end Russia's four-and-a-half-year war in Ukraine.
Kushner and Witkoff travelled from Moscow, where they held three hours of talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Saturday but did not appear to secure a breakthrough in the conflict.
Previous rounds of U.S.-mediated peace talks encouraged by President Donald Trump, who campaigned on a promise to quickly end the war, have yielded few results. He suggested on Friday that the U.S. had a fresh proposal, though he did not elaborate.
Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov described Saturday's meeting as "highly useful," while a White House official told Reuters that next steps would be announced in the coming weeks.
The two envoys met Zelenskiy and other top Ukrainian officials in central Kyiv.
Zelenskiy, who believes Washington will be key to any peace deal, has said a window of opportunity to make peace exists before the U.S. begins focusing on its next presidential election.
After the first round of talks between Ukrainian and U.S. negotiators that lasted about three hours, the U.S. envoys said that they were looking forward to making more progress.
"Substantive, important, and we are very encouraged,” Witkoff told reporters after the talks, which also included a working lunch.
Zelenskiy said that more talks, which would also include European representatives, were planned later on Sunday. British, French and German national security advisers were in Kyiv on Sunday.
"Security guarantees are needed. A dignified post-war peace is needed. Our proposals have been drawn up," Zelenskiy said as his negotiating team was preparing to meet U.S. envoys.
Cautious optimism on the streets of Kyiv
Witkoff and Kushner, Trump's son-in-law, have visited Moscow several times in their roles as peace envoys. But Sunday is their first visit to Kyiv in their capacity as U.S. negotiators.
Their visit has long been sought by Ukraine's leadership, and on the streets of Kyiv, which has been bombarded heavily in recent weeks, some residents were hopeful.
"The issue can be solved in the blink of an eye. We want peace. I've fought myself, so I know what war is like. We need peace, because there's no other way," said military veteran Stepan Yermak.
In previous talks, the sides have remained far apart on key issues, including the future of the eastern Ukrainian region of Donbas. Russia has demanded Ukraine's withdrawal from an entrenched belt of towns that it still controls there, but Kyiv has refused, reasoning that it can still hold on.
For Ukraine, hard security guarantees from its European allies and the U.S. are crucial to deterring Russia from invading again.
"We need an agreement that will never be broken," said Svitlana Kurylenko, a 19-year-old cafe worker.
"Just leave Ukraine alone and let people live in peace."
Temporary halt in strikes
Though the front lines of the ground war remain largely static, both Russian and Ukrainian forces have intensified long-range air strikes in recent weeks.
Russia has pounded the Ukrainian capital day and night with missiles and drones for the past two weeks, including an attack on Friday on the headquarters of the SBU security service.
The Kremlin has said it would pause strikes on Kyiv until Monday, while Zelenskiy has said Ukraine would also halt strikes on Moscow.
There was no let-up in fighting along the 1,200-kilometer (750-mile) front, however, and Russia bombarded other Ukrainian cities on Saturday.
Ukraine has inflicted damaging hits throughout the summer on Russian refineries, oil terminals and the warehouses of online retailer Wildberries, in an attempt to raise the cost to Moscow of continuing the war.
Ukraine said on Sunday it had struck the Ryazan oil refinery, around 480 kilometers (300 miles) inside Russia, overnight, causing a fire.

articles.title: Air Force Capability Coalition Identifies Helicopters as Priority for Aid to Ukraine
articles.body:
The Air Force Capability Coalition has identified the development of Ukraine’s helicopter capabilities as one of five priority areas for further assistance to Ukraine.
The Ministry of Defence of Ukraine reported this.
The issue was discussed during a meeting of the Secretariat and working groups of the Air Force Capability Coalition in Kyiv. Representatives of Ukraine, the Netherlands, Denmark, the United States, the United Kingdom and Canada took part in the meeting.
Earlier, it was reported that the Ukrainian Ground Forces’ Army Aviation plans to receive U.S.-made UH-60 Black Hawk helicopters to replace Soviet-era helicopters.
In addition to developing helicopter capabilities, the partners will focus on developing aviation infrastructure, training personnel, maintaining existing aviation capabilities, and expanding defense-industrial and military-technical cooperation.
Mi-17 helicopters of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, June 2023. Photo: Joint Forces Command of the Armed Forces of Ukraine
The meeting participants also separately discussed the creation of an Air Force Capability Coalition Fund. It is intended to improve coordination among countries and help attract funding.
The Air Force Capability Coalition was established in 2023 as part of the Ukraine Defense Contact Group in the Ramstein format. It currently includes 14 countries.
The coalition’s work covers more than the transfer of fighter aircraft to Ukraine. The partners also assist with training pilots, engineers and technicians, supplying aviation weapons, developing airfield infrastructure and repair capabilities, and providing protected shelters.
Under this framework, Ukraine has already received F-16 and Mirage 2000 fighter jets. Cooperation with Sweden on JAS 39 Gripen fighter jets is also underway.
Another area is the training of Ukrainian aviation personnel. For this purpose, partners are providing mobile F-16 simulators, while the Czech Republic uses L-39 trainer aircraft and Alto NG light aircraft to train Ukrainian pilots.
An important component of the future system is Sweden’s ASC 890 airborne early warning and control aircraft. It can detect aerial targets at considerable distances and transmit information to coordinate aviation operations.
At the same time, the Ministry of Defense of Ukraine has not yet specified which helicopter platforms or programs are planned to be developed as part of the identified priority.
Earlier, in 2024, German company HENSOLDT received a contract to supply protection systems for Ukrainian helicopters.
The development of helicopter capabilities is expected to become part of a broader transformation of Ukraine’s Air Force along Western standards, together with combat aviation, reconnaissance, personnel training, weapons and aviation infrastructure.

articles.title: US Envoys Hold Three-Hour Kremlin Talks With Putin
articles.body:
US special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held more than three hours of talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Saturday evening, Sept. 5, presenting proposals on potential pathways to end the war against Ukraine.
The meeting at the Kremlin lasted three hours and 10 minutes and included formal discussions followed by an informal working dinner, according to Putin aide Yuri Ushakov.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
Putin was joined by Ushakov and Russian special representative for economic cooperation Kirill Dmitriev, who characterized the trip on social media as an “important peacemaking visit.”
A White House official told Reuters that the negotiations were “meaningful,” adding that the next steps in the diplomatic process would be announced in the coming weeks.
Ushakov stated that the US envoys arrived “seriously prepared” and presented concrete ideas for a settlement.
However, the Kremlin reiterated its standard demands regarding the conflict, emphasizing battlefield positions and the need to address what Moscow terms the “root causes” of the war. Ushakov added that the US delegation agreed to take Putin’s assessments into account during their scheduled meetings in Kyiv.
Beyond the war in Ukraine, the discussions covered broader bilateral economic relations, including potential large-scale, mutually beneficial US-Russian commercial projects.
Serbia Is Not a Russian Province, and Lavrov Has No Right to Decide Its Future
Ushakov noted that Putin and US President Donald Trump intend to maintain direct personal contact and that working channels involving Witkoff and Kushner will remain active.
Important peacemaking visit. 🕊️ pic.twitter.com/r5UQhjeMxE
— Kirill Dmitriev (@kadmitriev) September 5, 2026
Diplomatic pause and preparations for Kyiv visit
At the start of the meeting, Putin addressed the security situation in the Ukrainian capital, stating that Russian forces had halted strikes on Kyiv starting at midnight on Sept. 5. Putin noted that the request for a temporary pause had been transmitted through official diplomatic and intelligence channels.
However, Putin explicitly rejected Ukraine’s call for a wider three-day ceasefire across the entire front line, asserting that Moscow had never agreed to such an arrangement.
“We will do everything that depends on us to ensure the safety of the negotiation process and the mediators,” Putin said, while noting that Ukrainian drone activity toward Russian territory had also decreased. Witkoff reportedly thanked Putin for agreeing to the pause on strikes affecting both capitals.
Witkoff and Kushner are scheduled to travel to Kyiv on Sunday, Sept. 6, to meet with President Volodymyr Zelensky.
Prior to the Moscow meeting, Zelensky confirmed that he had spoken directly with Trump’s envoys, pledging that Ukrainian forces would refrain from launching aerial strikes against Moscow through the end of Monday to safeguard the diplomatic process.
While Ukraine had advocated for a comprehensive bilateral ceasefire, the Armed Forces of Ukraine confirmed that frontline combat operations remain ongoing elsewhere after Moscow rejected the broader truce.

Ukraine Reportedly Hits Russian Ship Carrying Iranian Weapons With 12 Drone Strikes
Ukraine reportedly carried out a drone attack against a sanctioned Russian cargo ship in the Mediterranean Sea, striking the vessel 12 times as it allegedly transported Iranian weapons and armored vehicles to Russia.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
According to reports published on September 6, the Russian-flagged Lady Maria was attacked by drones equipped with systems for dropping munitions while sailing in the Mediterranean. Footage circulating online appears to show multiple strikes against the vessel, followed by a fire on board.
Russian opposition journalist Alexander Nevzorov, who published footage of the attack, claimed that Lady Maria sustained 12 direct hits and that the drones were launched from Libyan territory. Neither Ukrainian authorities nor other official sources have confirmed Ukraine’s involvement in the attack. The reported contents of the vessel’s cargo and the claim that the drones were launched from Libya have also not been independently verified.
Ship-tracking data showed that Lady Maria, IMO 9220641, had departed the Algerian port of Oran before sailing into the Mediterranean. Recent tracking information placed the vessel near Sicily, while earlier route data indicated that it had passed near Crete in the direction of Syria.
The ship, currently named LADY MARIIA, is under US sanctions and was originally designated under its former name, STELLA-MARIA, due to its connection to Russian shipping company MG-Flot LLC, formerly known as TransMorFlot LLC. Ukraine also sanctioned the vessel on May 23, 2026.
Ukraine’s Defense Intelligence (HUR) identifies Lady Maria as a vessel involved in transporting military cargo and weapons for Russia. According to HUR, the ship has operated on the Novorossiysk–Tartus route and has previously been linked to transporting weapons from Syria to Russia.

articles.title: General Staff: Russia has lost 1,496,440 troops in Ukraine since Feb. 24, 2022
articles.body:
Russia has lost around 1,496,440 troops in Ukraine since the beginning of its full-scale invasion on Feb. 24, 2022, the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine reported on Sept. 6.
The figure includes 1,390 casualties that Russian forces suffered over the past day.
According to the report, Russia has also lost 12,331 tanks, 25,278 armored combat vehicles, 144,435 vehicles and fuel tanks, 49,260 artillery systems, 2,096 multiple launch rocket systems, 1,605 air defense systems, 441 aircraft, 355 helicopters, 2,507 unmanned ground systems, 501,244 aerial drones, 35 ships and boats, and two submarines.
Ukraine's General Staff has not revealed its own losses during the full-scale invasion, citing operational secrecy.
Independent Western think-tank reports agree that the Russian casualties significantly surpass Ukraine's losses, with the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) estimating the ratio to be "roughly 2.5:1 or 2:1."
A January 2026 CSIS report said Ukraine has likely suffered between 500,000 and 600,000 casualties from February 2022 to December 2025, of which between 100,000 and 140,000 are thought to be killed in action (KIA).
While Ukrainian officials rarely disclose the figure, President Volodymyr Zelensky told France TV on Feb. 4 that at least 55,000 Ukrainian soldiers have been killed in action since the beginning of the full-scale war, in addition to a lot more missing in action (MIAs).
The intensity of Russian drone attacks and the fighting has made it extremely difficult for Ukraine to retrieve the bodies of fallen soldiers, which are needed for DNA confirmation.

articles.title: France can’t finance Ukraine forever – Le Pen party head
articles.body:
France can’t finance Ukraine forever – Le Pen party head
France lacks money for itself and simply cannot keep funding Ukraine indefinitely, Jordan Bardella, the president of Marine Le Pen’s right-wing National Rally (NR) party, has said.
The main French opposition party faced harsh criticism from its rivals earlier this week after its vice president, Louis Aliot, said that NR “would turn off the tap” for Kiev if it comes to power after the 2027 presidential vote. Le Pen is seen as having strong chances to succeed in the election next year, no matter who her rival will be in the second round.
Bardella weighed in on the issue during his speech at the Ambrosetti Forum in Italy on Saturday, saying that Ukraine needs support from France and other Western nations during the conflict with Russia, but “our objective should not be to finance the war ad vitam æternam,” which means ‘forever’ in Latin.
France has a national debt of €3.5 trillion ($4.6 billion) and cannot be “giving money that we no longer have” to Vladimir Zelensky’s government, he argued.
“The extremely serious and worrying state of French public finances means we can’t give money without any guarantees or assurances that this money will be repaid one day,” the National Rally president said.
Paris has been one of the strongest backers of Kiev in the EU after the escalation of the Ukraine conflict in February 2022, providing it with billions in military aid and supplying various sophisticated weapons, including CAESAR self-propelled howitzers and Mirage fighter jets.
According to Bardella, the Americans were “much smarter” than the Europeans when it came to assistance for Kiev “because the money they gave to Ukraine is secured against rare earth mining.” He was referring to the deal agreed upon between Washington and Kiev last year, which grants the US preferential access to Ukrainian mineral resources.
During US President Donald Trump’s second term, Washington also significantly reduced aid to Ukraine, making European NATO members pay for American-made arms supplied to the country.
Earlier this week, Trump warned that he intends to present Europe with a belated bill for billions of dollars that Washington spent arming Ukraine under his predecessor, Joe Biden. He previously estimated that Biden gave Zelensky more than $300 billion worth of weapons for “free.”
Le Pen said on Thursday that the National Rally is skeptical about further assistance to Ukraine because it believes that the conflict with Russia needs a diplomatic solution.
A poll by Harris Interactive in late August suggested that Le Pen has the support of 34% of the French public, which should guarantee her a place in the second round of the presidential election, where she would likely win comfortably against either her left-wing rival Jean-Luc Mélenchon or the centrist candidate, former Prime Minister Edouard Philippe.
Russian officials said repeatedly that foreign weapons being sent to Kiev will not prevent Moscow from achieving its military goals, but will merely prolong the fighting, while increasing the risk of a direct confrontation between Russia and NATO.

articles.title: Ukraine’s drone forces say they hit 58,465 Russian targets in August, nearly 1,900 a day. Three named campaigns did the strategic damage
articles.body:
Ukraine's drone forces say they struck 58,465 Russian targets in August, an average of nearly 1,900 a day. The tally is up almost 9 percent on July and more than double January's, and it included 54 vessels of Russia's shadow fleet, 33 air-defense systems, and 168 energy nodes, Unmanned Systems Forces commander Robert "Madiar" Brovdi reported on his Telegram channel.
The volume matters less than where some of it lands. Cutting power to occupied Crimea and the south is meant to blind Russian air defense, much of which runs on the grid. Meanwhile, the strikes on Russia's sanctions-evading shadow fleet squeeze both Crimea's fuel supply and Moscow's oil exports.
Ukraine's drone forces claim 11,010 Russian troop casualties in August
Brovdi also said the strikes killed or wounded 11,010 Russian soldiers over the month, about 355 a day — a figure that counts only losses the drone force attributes to its own strikes, not Russia's total casualties.
That daily rate was slightly below July's 374, down about 5 percent, even as the number of targets rose. Compared with January, the force said Russian personnel losses were up 17.3 percent.
Three campaigns inside the count
Most of the headline volume is small front-line targets, but three named operations account for the strategic hits. Under Operation "Milk", the force said it struck 54 shadow-fleet vessels in August, bringing the total to 260 since the campaign began on 6 July. Operation "PPOpad" — a play on the Ukrainian for air defense — hit 33 Russian air-defense elements in August and 263 across 2026.
The third, Operation "Crimean Switch Off", struck 168 energy nodes in August, bringing the total to 349 since early July. That campaign has been running for months, blacking out swaths of occupied Crimea.
Brovdi has argued that cutting power to stationary radars and other air-defense elements opens the airspace for deeper Ukrainian strikes. Months of these strikes have left occupied Crimea rationing fuel and living with rolling blackouts, and cut the Kerch ferry crossing's capacity by about three-quarters. All of the figures are the force's own, and Ukraine's military claims of Russian losses are not independently verified.

articles.title: US offers ‘substantive plan’ to end Ukraine war
articles.body:
Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky (L) welcomes US Special Envoys Steve Witkoff (R) and Jared Kushner (C) prior to their talks in Kyiv on September 6, 2026, amid the Russian invasion of Ukraine. (AFP Photo)
U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff were in Kiev on Sept. 6 for their first visit to the Ukrainian capital, a day after discussed “substantive plans” with Russia’s Vladimir Putin in the Kremlin on ending more than four years of war between the neighbors.
U.S. President Donald Trump’s business partner Witkoff and son-in-law Kushner had visited Moscow several times but had not held talks in Kiev, hit by deadly Russian strikes since 2022.
Witkoff and Kushner met with Putin on Sept. 5 to “advance President Trump’s agenda of peace in the Russia-Ukraine War,” a White House official said.
“The two sides discussed substantive plans for next steps, which will be announced in the coming weeks, and look forward to equally productive meetings tomorrow in Ukraine.”
Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov called the talks “extremely frank”, saying the Americans “put forward a number of ideas on possible routes to a settlement,” but did not elaborate.
The Russian side told the Americans that Moscow was “confident” it could achieve its military goals of seizing the rest of eastern Ukraine, Ushakov added.
Both Russia and Ukraine have vowed not to strike each other’s capitals for three days to allow for the negotiations to take place.
In televised comments before the talks, Putin said Russia would ensure the safety of the envoys in Kiev, a city Moscow has pounded with deadly strikes throughout the war.
“We will do everything that depends on us to ensure the safety of the negotiation process and mediators such as yourselves,” Putin told Witkoff and Kushner.
Earlier on Sept. 5, Putin had thanked Trump for persisting in his efforts to end the war despite it being “not simple.”
Of the envoys’ trip to Kiev, he said: “No matter what happens next, contacts of this kind are undoubtedly always beneficial.”
Trump said on Sept. 4 his envoys were bringing a “proposal” to end fighting.
“We have an idea for peace,” he said, without elaborating.
U.S. efforts have so far not led to a breakthrough in the war, and peace efforts have stalled in part because of Washington’s war with Iran.
Russia occupied large swathes of eastern and southern Ukraine, and Putin has insisted Moscow is intent on seizing the rest of eastern Ukraine.
Both Moscow and Kiev committed to suspending strikes as the negotiations took place.
“The Russian president, the commander-in-chief, has given the order from midnight not to strike Kyiv for three days,” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said.
Zelensky said he had spoken to the U.S. envoys and also promised Kiev would not strike Moscow.
However, Kiev said that Russian strikes had killed 10 people across the country on Sept. 5, including a child and his family members in the Kharkiv region and two people outside Kiev.
Zelensky accused Moscow of trying to disrupt the visit of the U.S. envoys with overnight attacks on Kiev’s two airports, as well as on civilian targets.

articles.title: Leonardo Seeks Partnerships With Ukrainian Defense Companies
articles.body:
Italian defense giant Leonardo, through its new Kyiv-based subsidiary, is looking for opportunities to partner with Ukrainian companies, as well as for potential investments or acquisitions.
Leonardo CEO Lorenzo Mariani said this in an interview with Bloomberg.
The Italian defense giant opened its Ukrainian subsidiary, Leonardo Ukraine, in August 2026. The company is registered in Kyiv and, according to the announcement, will focus primarily on research and development (R&D) activities.
“The Ukrainian ecosystem of small and medium-sized companies and startups has both the opportunity and the ingenuity to develop highly innovative and well-tested solutions. Bringing these solutions together directly on the ground is the right way forward for further development,” Mariani said.
The Ukrainian subsidiary will also support the development of Leonardo’s Michelangelo air defense system. Mariani confirmed earlier plans to conduct the first tests in Ukraine by the end of 2026.
According to Mariani, Leonardo is already testing the system’s counter-drone component in Italy, while in Ukraine it initially plans to deploy the artillery layer of Michelangelo.
Michelangelo is already being offered to foreign customers seeking protection against drones and ballistic threats. According to Mariani, Leonardo is primarily targeting existing customers that already use the company’s sensors, as it is easier to demonstrate to them the benefits of integrating these capabilities into a broader system.
The Michelangelo Dome is a prospective layered air and missile defense system being developed by Leonardo. Its concept envisions integrating radars, electro-optical sensors, electronic warfare (EW) systems, artillery, missile systems, aircraft, and space-based early-warning systems into a single network.
A key element of the system is intended to be a unified command-and-information architecture that will receive data from multiple sensors and automatically select the most suitable effector for a specific target. This approach is intended to enable more effective engagement of both individual threats and massed, coordinated attacks.
The lower tier of the Michelangelo Dome is primarily designed to counter unmanned aerial systems (UAS) and other low-altitude, low-cost targets. For this purpose, Leonardo is considering the use of 30 mm, 40 mm, and 76 mm gun systems integrated with radars, electro-optical systems, and electronic warfare capabilities.
The upper tiers of the system are intended to counter aircraft as well as cruise, ballistic, and hypersonic missiles. To achieve this, the Michelangelo Dome is planned to be integrated with radars from the KRONOS and RAT 31 families, along with other sensors and air and missile defense systems.
A dedicated space-based early-warning layer is also planned as part of the Michelangelo Dome, based on the Space Guardian satellite constellation. The first group of satellites is planned for launch in late 2027 or early 2028, with the second group scheduled for late 2028 or early 2029. Initial operational capability of the constellation is expected in 2028, with full operational capability targeted for 2029.
The satellite-based sensors are designed to detect missile launches by identifying the characteristic thermal signature of their engines and transmit the data to a ground-based command-and-control system. The latter would then refine the missile’s trajectory using radar data and task the appropriate interceptor. This architecture is intended to increase the available reaction time, particularly against ballistic and hypersonic threats.

Ukraine Blinds Russian Defenses in Bryansk, Hitting Radar, EW System and MESH Network
Ukrainian forces struck several Russian military systems in Russia’s Bryansk region, including a radar station, an electronic warfare complex, and a relay supporting a MESH communications network.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
According to Ukraine’s General Staff on September 5, the strikes were carried out on September 4 and targeted military infrastructure at three separate locations across the region.
A Russian radar station was hit near Kartushino, while an electronic warfare system was targeted in the area of Pogar. Ukrainian forces also struck a MESH network relay in Zlynka, the General Staff said.
The General Staff did not identify the specific models of the radar or electronic warfare systems involved, meaning their exact capabilities and value cannot yet be independently assessed.
Radar stations are used for tasks ranging from airspace surveillance and target detection to supporting air defense and other military operations. Electronic warfare systems can be employed to detect, disrupt, or suppress radio communications, navigation signals, and drone control links.
The MESH relay represents a different part of the communications infrastructure. In a mesh network, individual nodes can relay data between one another rather than relying exclusively on a single central communications point.
Such architecture can extend communications coverage and provide alternative routes for data if individual links are disrupted. The General Staff did not specify which Russian MESH system was targeted or what units it supported.
Ukrainian forces also struck a repair facility used by a Russian military unit in Sokolohirsk in the temporarily occupied Luhansk region.
“The extent of the damage is being clarified. Work on the enemy’s key military targets continues. More to come!” Ukraine’s General Staff said.

articles.title: 3 vessels returned from Hormuz Strait after being warned by Iran's IRGC -- media

TEHRAN, Sept. 6 (Xinhua) -- Three vessels, including two oil tankers and a liquefied natural gas (LNG) carrier, changed course and turned back while seeking to transit the Strait of Hormuz via a southern route after receiving warnings from the navy of Iran's Islamic Revolution Guard Corps (IRGC), media reported Sunday.
Citing the latest maritime tracking data, the semi-official Fars news agency identified the vessels as Marshall Islands-flagged oil tanker Velos Amber, Liberian-flagged oil tanker BRAVO and Marshall Islands-flagged LNG tanker AL SHEEHANIYA, which belongs to Qatar.
It added that the IRGC's Navy had warned the three tankers that the southern route in the strait was closed.
The development comes amid a series of naval confrontations between Iran and the United States.
U.S. Central Command said Saturday on social media platform X that U.S. forces had struck three Iranian crude oil carriers after the IRGC "launched ballistic missiles toward two U.S. Navy warships patrolling regional waters."
The IRGC Navy later confirmed the U.S. strikes, saying it had targeted three oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and three U.S.-affiliated vessels elsewhere in retaliation.

articles.title: Ex-Pentagon chief anticipates US-Iran standoff to continues for six months more
articles.body:
LONDON, September 6. /TASS/. The armed conflict between the United States and Iran may continue for six months more, former Pentagon chief (2011-2013) and former CIA director (2009-2011) Leon Panetta said.
"I think the likelihood is this war is going to continue for another six months without being resolved," he said in an interview with The Guardian.
"It’s no mystery that the United States and Iran are caught in a terrible stalemate, in which there really are very few options available to bring this war to an end," he said, adding that the Trump administration is risking to be dragged into a protracted war in the Middle East.
According to Panetta, the conflict seems to be on course to become "another failed war" in the Middle East "like Iraq and Afghanistan." The United States’ adversaries "see weakness in terms of our ability to be able to really implement our military capability of defending our country," he noted.
US President Donald Trump, in his words has "boxed himself in" and now has three options: to "admit that it’s a failed war" and walk away, which he thinks to be highly improbable; to continue exchanging strikes, with both sides attempting to "avoid the startup of a more dangerous war" but refusing to negotiate or surrender, which he believes will lead to a protracted war; and to finally take control of the Strait of Hormuz and this way strip Iran of its "most dangerous leverage point" over the US.
The United States and Israel launched a war against Iran on February 28. In June, Washington and Tehran signed a memorandum of understanding envisaging an immediate ceasefire on all fronts, including in Lebanon. However, the United States resumed large-scale attacks on Iran overnight to July 8, having accused it of breaching the existing agreements in what concerned the Strait of Hormuz, a global chokepoint for approximately 25% of oil and some 20% of LNG supplies.
The Trump administration recently signaled an end to any large-scale use of force against Iran and a transition to putting economic pressure on the Islamic Republic through sanctions instead.

articles.title: Germany prepares comprehensive "protective shield" against Russian sabotage
articles.body:
Germany prepares comprehensive "protective shield" against Russian sabotage
Following a failed attempt to attack Leipzig/Halle airport with an explosive-laden drone, Germany plans to strengthen protection against Russian sabotage and other hybrid attacks.
Source: German tabloid Bild, as reported by European Pravda
Details: German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt is planning a package of measures covering protection against drones and sabotage targeting critical infrastructure and cyberattacks, as well as the detection of spies and potential terrorists.
"Russia's hybrid attacks using explosive-laden drones targeting airports, agents in our cities, cyberattacks on our networks and sabotage of our infrastructure are a daily reality. These attacks will intensify, but we can fight back and protect ourselves," Dobrindt said.
According to Bild, Germany plans to expand the Federal Police's mobile anti-drone unit.
The new units, which can be rapidly deployed to different areas, will have helicopters and special vehicles. They will be stationed in nine strategically important cities: Frankfurt am Main, Munich, Hamburg, Berlin, Stuttgart, Düsseldorf, Leipzig, Hanover and Cologne.
Their task will be to protect the airspace above key transport hubs, airports, railway stations and the government district in Berlin. This will involve not only detecting and intercepting drones, but also disabling explosive-laden UAVs.
Another proposal involves expanding the powers of companies operating critical infrastructure. Water utilities, energy companies and defence industry facilities could be given legal powers not only to detect drones but also to actively counter them. This should allow them to respond more quickly to attacks on critical infrastructure facilities without waiting for state forces to arrive.
The plan also envisages wider use of AI, biometric facial recognition and video surveillance systems, particularly at railway stations. AI would help automatically detect weapons and suspicious behaviour, as well as identify people suspected of preparing attacks or engaging in espionage.
Another area is protection against cyberattacks. The plan calls for the creation of a national Cyberdome – an extensive network of digital sensors designed to detect and block attempted hacker attacks.
Background: On 1 September, Germany directly accused Russia of a hybrid attack at Leipzig airport in early August and announced countermeasures.
